heading: Creating a page
text:
## Creating a page Add a page by exporting a default component from `page.tsx`. The route is the folder name, so `app/dashboard/page.tsx` renders at `/dashboard`. Keep the file small: data fetching belongs in a server component above it (PAGE-MARK). ```tsx // app/dashboard/page.tsx # not a heading: this line sits inside a fence export default function Page() { return

Dashboard

} ```

heading: Layouts and Pages
text:
Layouts and Pages

A page is the UI that is unique to a route. A layout is UI shared across many
routes. In the App Router both are React components, and the file system decides
where each one renders. This preamble sits before the first heading and must
become its own section, titled from the frontmatter above (PREAMBLE-MARK).

heading: Long section
text:
## Long section

This section exists to exceed the two-thousand-character grouping cap. The
splitter groups whole paragraphs up to the cap and labels the overflow with a
`(part 2)` heading, so a long run of prose never produces a chunk wider than the
embedding budget allows. Everything here is filler with one marker per paragraph
so a test can prove no paragraph was dropped (LONG-P1). A documentation section
that runs long is normal: configuration tables, lists of caveats and migration
notes all push a single heading well past the cap. The splitter answers that by
cutting at paragraph boundaries only. It never cuts mid-sentence, never cuts
inside a fence, and never rewrites the source: the bytes of every paragraph
survive in exactly the order the author wrote them, with a part number added to
the heading of the continuation chunk so a reader knows the section continues.

The second paragraph repeats the same point with different wording, because a
real documentation page does exactly that: it states the rule once, restates it
for the reader who skimmed, then supplies an example that shows the rule in
action. What matters for the corpus is that paragraph boundaries are the only
cut points used here, and that the text before and after the cut is preserved
verbatim. A chunk that silently loses a sentence is worse than a chunk that is
too long, because the retriever then cites a paragraph that no longer says what
the question assumed (LONG-P2). The grouping step adds paragraphs to a group
while the rendered body stays under the cap, then starts a new group. That means
a long section becomes a small number of wide chunks rather than many narrow
ones, which keeps the embedding of each chunk coherent.

heading: Long section (part 2)
text:
## Long section (part 2)

The third paragraph closes the section. A reader who lands on the split part
still sees the heading it belongs to, and the part number tells them the section
continues. Nothing is summarised, reordered or reflowed: the splitter is a pure
function over the source markdown (LONG-P3). Run it twice over the same bytes and
the same sections come back in the same order, which is what keeps chunk ids
stable between builds and lets an eval query keep pointing at the same text.

heading: Retrieving data
text:
## Short note

A deliberately short note (SHORT-MARK).


## Retrieving data

Fetch data in the component that needs it. An async server component may await
the request directly, and the result is streamed to the client as the tree
resolves. Cache with `fetch` options when the answer can be reused, and revalidate
on a timer when it cannot (DATA-MARK).

heading: Matcher
text:
## Matcher

The matcher accepts path patterns and runs only on matching requests. A matcher
that misses nested routes is the usual cause of a middleware that "does not
run", which is why the synthetic forum answer for this topic is labelled stale
(MATCHER-MARK).

heading: Usage
text:
## Usage

Export a function that returns a response or calls `next()`. The matcher limits
which requests enter the function; without a matcher every request pays the
cost. Middleware runs on the edge runtime, so it cannot open a database socket
or read the file system (USAGE-MARK).

heading: middleware
text:
middleware

Middleware runs before a request reaches a route. It lives at the project root
in `middleware.ts` and exports one function and an optional matcher. This
fixture path is the one the committed rule table marks as superseded, so the
label must come from the rule and not from the path default (MIDDLEWARE-MARK).

heading: Caveats
text:
## Caveats

A page may export one data-fetching function. Mixing `getStaticProps` and
`getServerSideProps` in the same file is an error, and the Pages Router refuses
the build rather than guessing which one the author meant (CAVEAT-MARK).

heading: Data Fetching
text:
Data Fetching

The Pages Router fetches data in exported functions rather than in the component
body. `getStaticProps` runs at build time, `getServerSideProps` runs on each
request, and both hand their result to the page component as props. This
preamble must stay a section of its own and label as pages/current (PAGES-MARK).

heading: Nested note
text:
### Nested note

A third-level heading must survive as its own section and keep its three-hash
prefix when rendered. This note is long enough that the merge step leaves it
alone, so the splitter renders it with `###` and the label default still comes
from the path, not from the heading text (NESTED-MARK).

heading: getServerSideProps
ISR revalidate not working
text: In Next 12.1 you set unstable_revalidate in getStaticProps. That key was removed; the current key is revalidate.
